title: Indian Bank - 532814 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Analyst / Investor Meet - Outcome

summary.headline: Indian Bank Q2 FY27 net profit rose 14.71% to Rs 3,462 crore, helped by Rs 1,134 crore NSE MTM gain; guidance raised to 11-12% deposit and 13-14% advances growth.
summary.overview: Indian Bank reported Q2 FY27 with total business up 14.22%, advances up 16.39% and deposits up 12.50% year on year. Profit was lifted by NSE-related gains (Rs 252 crore realised plus Rs 1,134 crore MTM), while operating profit excluding NSE grew about 18%. Management raised deposit and advances growth guidance, and flagged ECL provisioning (Rs 1,500 crore this quarter, Rs 2,500 crore cumulative) and a possible one-time HTM mark-to-market hit from 1 April. CASA ratio improved year on year to 39.36% but slipped sequentially on FCNR(B) inflows.

financial_highlights.value: Not stated in total; includes NSE gains of Rs 252 crore realised and Rs 1,134 crore MTM

financial_highlights.change: +8 bps YoY; domestic +1 bp QoQ, global +2 bps QoQ
Up from 38.87% YoY; slightly down QoQ
Down from Rs 1.62 lakh crore QoQ

segments.name: Retail
segments.commentary: Retail advances grew 17.37% YoY; 92% of the retail book has CIBIL score above 750. Housing originated 60% via branches and 40% via DSAs, with zero co-lending.

segments.name: Agriculture
segments.commentary: Agriculture advances grew 17.18% YoY. Agri gold loan book reached Rs 1.16 lakh crore, up about 22% YoY and 11% QoQ. Agri book outside drought-declared states is under Rs 1,000 crore.

segments.name: MSME
segments.commentary: MSME advances grew 19.06% YoY. About Rs 10,000 crore of MSME limits remains undrawn.

segments.name: Corporate
segments.commentary: Corporate advances grew 9.92% YoY. Pipeline of Rs 63,000 crore: Rs 30,000 crore sanctioned but undisbursed, Rs 10,000 crore in-principle approved, around Rs 23,000 crore early stage. Growth target now 10-12%.

segments.name: RAM
segments.commentary: RAM advances grew 17.74% YoY and constitute about 67% of the loan book.

segments.name: Treasury
segments.commentary: Treasury income ex-NSE was Rs 290 crore in Q2 (Rs 293 crore a year ago) and Rs 794 crore in H1 (Rs 854 crore). Net MTM loss of about Rs 11 crore. Management expects muted treasury income going forward.

segments.name: International book
segments.commentary: Loans against FCNR(B) deposits of about USD 2 billion were extended at preferential rates, with customers borrowing 90-96% of deposit value; this drove advances growth and is expected not to recur fully next quarter.

guidance_outlook: Deposit growth guidance raised to 11-12% from 9-11%.
Advances growth guidance raised to 13-14% from 11-13%; during Q&A CEO said 14-15% for next quarter and 12-13% in another comment.
NIM expected to expand 5-6 bps in Q3 FY27 (6-7 bps in one response); further moves depend on repo rate.
Recovery guidance unchanged; management expects to do better than guided.
Recurring ECL impact on credit cost maintained at 10-15 bps; one-time ECL impact expected at Rs 3,500 crore in total.
CRAR expected at around 17-17.5% by March-end; Rs 1,000-2,000 crore Tier 2 raise possible in January after Rs 1,000 crore maturity.
Bulk deposits to be raised cautiously; up to Rs 5,000 crore infrastructure bonds approved; CASA ratio target around 40%.
capex_capacity: Corporate credit capacity being built; corporate growth was 1-2% earlier, now targeted at 10-12% with credit training.

CRM launched in July added about Rs 1,500 crore of business in the quarter; fintech solutions to 223 companies and government departments added about Rs 5,000 crore; CMS-linked CASA about Rs 7,000 crore.
AI tools launched in Q2: TARA voice-based conversational banking and Smart Wealth personal finance tool; digital business grew 18% YoY.
Added about 2.5 lakh salary accounts this year so far against 3 lakh in full last year.
demand_pricing: Competition very high across segments; many banks lending housing below 7%. Management not chasing 20-25% growth, citing bottom-line and underwriting risk.
MCLR-linked book is 43.19% of advances; external benchmark-linked book is 49.65%. Benefit of 25 bp repo hike accrued from next day on external-linked loans.
Agri gold loan yield 8.85% (one-year MCLR), unchanged QoQ.
Working capital demand is stagnant: WCDL down Rs 1,000-2,000 crore and cash credit down Rs 1,000-2,000 crore over two to three quarters; management sees no crisis-led drawdown increase.
No stress seen in SME, agriculture or retail; SMA-2 accounts above Rs 25 crore total only about Rs 400 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Why did standard asset provisions rise from Rs 733 crore to Rs 1,882 crore, and what drove miscellaneous income to Rs 468 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: ECL provision of Rs 1,500 crore this quarter and Rs 1,000 crore last quarter, totalling Rs 2,500 crore, against an expected total impact of Rs 3,500 crore. Other income includes Rs 271 crore of interest on an income tax refund, which may not recur.

qa_highlights.question: Where will treasury income come from?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects muted treasury income and does not expect high profits; not budgeted for high treasury gains. Forex income guidelines from RBI are being assessed.

qa_highlights.question: Will deposit and credit growth continue, and what drives NIM?
qa_highlights.answer: 12% deposit growth expected to be maintained; advances growth of 14-15% expected next quarter. NIM to rise 6-7 bps (later framed as 5-6 bps) this quarter, with bulk deposits repricing later.

qa_highlights.question: How much FCNR(B) was raised and how much is lent against it?
qa_highlights.answer: USD 2.3 billion (about Rs 21,000 crore) raised; fully utilised, with no surplus liquidity. Loans against it of roughly USD 2 billion, with customers borrowing 90-96% of deposit value.

qa_highlights.question: What is the ECL recurring impact and is it passed on through pricing?
qa_highlights.answer: Recurring impact of 10-15 bps maintained. Management does not expect clear pass-through to borrowers; models take 1.5-2 years to stabilise. LGD uses five years of history.

qa_highlights.question: What is the HTM mark-to-market exposure and could RBI provide an HTM reserve?
qa_highlights.answer: The Rs 3,500 crore covers only the credit book; HTM MTM would be additional, and the 10-year yield at 7.41% could cause a large impact across banks. Bank will first take it up with RBI.

qa_highlights.question: What is the impact of UCC guidelines on capital?
qa_highlights.answer: One-time CET1 and Tier 2 adjustment, with unutilised limits now included in credit RWA. CRAR at 16.21%, expected at 17-17.5% by March-end.

qa_highlights.question: What drives the borrowing increase and the LCR?
qa_highlights.answer: Only USD 400 million OFCB raised, no MTNs. Borrowings through repo and TREPS rose; OFCB funding at about Rs 10,000-11,000 crore is expected to remain. LCR 116%, with lower excess SLR affecting the ratio.

risks_watch: Recurring ECL impact of 10-15 bps on credit cost is maintained, but management says models take 1.5-2 years to stabilise and pass-through to borrowers is unlikely; watch credit cost against this range.
One-time ECL impact is expected at about Rs 3,500 crore in total, of which Rs 2,500 crore was provided in H1; the remaining Rs 1,000 crore is still to come.
HTM mark-to-market from 1 April is unresolved: the Rs 3,500 crore covers only the credit book, HTM MTM would be additional, and the bank will first approach RBI on possible relief.

FCNR(B) inflows of USD 2.3 billion are fully deployed into loans against deposits (about USD 2 billion) at preferential rates, and management expects this to not recur fully next quarter, so advances growth may slow.
NIM expansion depends on repo rate moves and on bulk deposit repricing; management is cautious on bulk deposits and CD rates have hardened recently.
Treasury income is expected to be muted; forex income guidelines from RBI are under assessment. Other income includes Rs 271 crore of one-time income tax refund interest.
LCR at 116% is affected by higher borrowings and lower excess SLR; OFCB funding of about Rs 10,000-11,000 crore is expected to stay on the book.
key_quotes: Treasury income will be muted going forward, and I do not expect very high profits from it.
So, 12% deposit growth is expected and we will be able to maintain.
It covers only the credit book. HTM will be over and above that, and we have to see.
I do not think Banks will be able to pass it on clearly, because some large loans are still being priced at very fine rates; passing it on will be very difficult.
summary.management_tone: Confident on asset quality, deposits and the NSE-driven profit, with stated comfort on CRAR and growth. Cautious and non-committal on NIM trajectory, HTM mark-to-market exposure and recurring ECL pass-through, where management said it would wait and watch and that the regulator may not accept all assumptions.

adds.what: CRM launched in July added about Rs 1,500 crore of business in the quarter (business addition, not productive capacity)

growth.why: Advances growth guidance raised to 13-14% and deposits to 11-12%, backed by a Rs 63,000 crore corporate pipeline (Rs 30,000 crore sanctioned but undisbursed), Rs 10,000 crore undrawn MSME limits and a 67% RAM book, though the brief gives no productive capacity additions and the CEO's Q&A quotes (14-15% next quarter, 12-13% elsewhere) are inconsistent.
